title: Shopify vs Square Online in Canada
description: Shopify vs Square Online for a Canadian shop that sells in person and online: CAD card rates, debit, sales tax set-up, French pages and getting your data out.
h1: Shopify vs Square Online for a Canadian shop with a counter and a website
name: Shopify vs Square Online
lead: Most owners weighing these two already take payments in person. Square started at the counter and added a website; Shopify started online and added point of sale. Which one fits depends on where most of your sales happen today and which half of the business you want the software to run best.
factsHeading: Shopify and Square Online at a glance

facts.label: Shopify: Basic plan
facts.value: $37 CAD/mo paid yearly, or $49 CAD/mo paid monthly

facts.label: Shopify: Canadian sales tax
facts.value: Shopify Tax covers GST, HST, PST, QST and RST; no fee until $100,000 CAD in lifetime sales

facts.label: Shopify: Interac e-Transfer
facts.value: Manual 'email money transfer' method for Canadian merchants; you mark the order paid after accepting the transfer

facts.label: Shopify: French storefront
facts.value: Translate & Adapt app, CSV files or a compatible third-party app

facts.label: Shopify: data export
facts.value: Products export to CSV; product images are not included

facts.label: Square Online: Free plan
facts.value: $0, no monthly fee; paid Plus and Premium plans are billed annually

facts.label: Square: online card rate (CAD)
facts.value: 2.8% + 30¢ per transaction; an additional 1.5% applies to cards issued outside Canada

facts.label: Square: in-person rates (CAD)
facts.value: Credit 2.5% per transaction; debit 0.75% + 7¢ per transaction

facts.label: Square: Canadian sales tax
facts.value: Automatic calculator charges tax based on the tax enrolments in your account and where the order is fulfilled; an enrolment is not a registration with a tax authority

facts.label: Square Online: French site
facts.value: Weglot for a multi-language site, or a separate site per language; translation is for Plus and Premium subscribers

facts.label: Square: data export
facts.value: Item library exports to Excel (.xlsx) or CSV

body: Square is at home on the counter. The card reader, the item library and the staff app come first, and Square Online is a website built on top of that library. If most of your revenue comes through the door, the website is mainly a way to take pickup orders and show the menu or product range.

Shopify is at home online. Collections, product filters, themes and the app store are built for a store where the website is the main till. Shopify POS joins the counter to the same inventory, and the POS Pro add-on costs $119 CAD a month per location if you need its extra retail features.
Ask yourself where the next sale is most likely to come from. That answer usually settles the choice faster than any feature list.

sections.h2: What each one costs to run
body: Square Online has a free plan with no monthly fee, so a café or a maker already on Square can put up an ordering site for nothing beyond processing. Paid Plus and Premium plans add features such as translation and are billed annually; the Canadian plans page shows their prices without a currency code, so confirm the CAD amount in your Square Dashboard before you upgrade.

Shopify Basic is $37 CAD a month paid yearly, or $49 paid monthly. There is no free plan for a full store, but you get a store built around selling online from day one, with checkout and abandoned-checkout tools included.

Online, the two start at the same headline rate in Canada: 2.8% + 30¢ per card transaction. Square adds 1.5% for cards issued outside Canada, which matters if you ship to American customers. Shopify's rate drops on higher plans.

In person, Square lists debit at 0.75% + 7¢ per transaction and credit at 2.5%. For a shop where many customers tap a debit card, that flat-plus-percentage debit rate is often the deciding number, so run a month of your real sales through both calculators.

Online Interac is less tidy. We found no built-in Interac checkout on either platform's Canadian online pages. Shopify supports Interac e-Transfer as a manual payment method that you confirm by hand. On Square Online, plan for customers to pay by card or wallet.

Square's automatic Canadian tax calculator charges tax based on the tax enrolments in your account and where the order is fulfilled. Square is clear that an enrolment only tells the till which rate to look up; it does not register you with the CRA or a province. Online fulfilment taxes are managed from the Square Dashboard, with separate overrides for delivery and pickup, so check those once your counter taxes are right.

Shopify Tax covers GST, HST, PST, QST and Manitoba's RST. It is free until a store passes $100,000 CAD in lifetime sales, then charges a small per-order fee. Shopify also leaves filing and remitting to you.

sections.h2: French pages and moving your data
body: On Square Online, a French site comes either from Weglot, which adds a language switcher and translates the whole site, or from running a separate site for each language. Both options are for Plus and Premium subscribers. Shopify translates through Translate & Adapt, CSV files or a compatible third-party app.

Square exports the item library to Excel or CSV, which covers the catalogue you use at the counter and online. Shopify exports products to CSV but leaves product images out of the file. Neither export carries the website design itself, so keep your own copies of photos and page text.

Square Online suits restaurants, cafés, salons and shops where the counter drives the business and the website takes pickup, delivery or simple orders. Starting free on the same item library is hard to beat.

Shopify suits retailers where the website is, or will soon be, the bigger channel: larger catalogues, shipping across Canada, product filters, and marketing apps. If you also run a counter, Shopify POS keeps stock in one place.

checklist: Total last month's sales by channel (counter, pickup, shipped) before choosing.
Run a month of real card and debit volume through each platform's rates.
Confirm your tax registrations first, then add matching enrolments or tax settings.
Test a full order in French if you serve Quebec or other French-speaking customers.
Export your item library or products today, so you know what a move would involve.

faqs.a: There is a free plan with no monthly fee. You still pay processing on every sale, and features such as site translation need a paid plan.

faqs.q: Can I use Square for the counter and Shopify for the website?
faqs.a: You can, but you would then run two catalogues and two inventories unless you add a connector. Most small shops are better off picking one system for both.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper for debit in person?
faqs.a: Square lists in-person debit at 0.75% + 7¢ per transaction. Compare that with the Shopify POS rate shown in your own admin, using your real average sale.

faqs.q: Does Square register me for PST?
faqs.a: No. A tax enrolment in Square only sets the rate at checkout. Registration with the CRA or a province is a separate step you take yourself.
